title: Re-run Jean case as acceptance test (case-agnostic criteria)
description: This is the real acceptance test. In production we get arbitrary disk images without knowing the case type, so the acceptance bar must be *artifact-centric*, not title-centric. A detector that only fires when the analyst already suspected exfiltration is useless. The bar is: given Jean's artifacts and no case-specific hints, does the engine surface the hash-identity correlation as a ranked finding?
acceptance_criteria:
All acceptance criteria are artifact-centric; no case-string matching.

- At least one finding is produced with:
  - `category == data_exfiltration` (from the fixed taxonomy, SFE-7)
  - `severity == CRITICAL`
  - `confidence >= 0.90`
  - evidence contains two independent SHA-256 values that are byte-equal (cross-artifact hash correlation)
  - evidence contains a save-to-send delta under 300 s
  - reasoning chain cites at least two independent artifact sources (e.g. MFT + PST)
- The finding ranks in the top 5 by confidence.
- The raw JSON is captured in `docs/real_examples/nps-2008-jean/engine_pass.md` for regression visibility.
- If confidence drops below 0.90 or the finding is not in the top 5, iterate on scoring, not on the acceptance bar.
- No acceptance criterion references the strings "Jean", "m57biz", "exfil", or "tuckgorge". The test must pass for any image exhibiting the same pattern.

title: Add EXFIL_CORRELATION contradiction type and detector
description: The new signal needs a home in the same detection/scoring pipeline the existing detectors use so findings appear in the same output shape, ranked alongside everything else.
acceptance_criteria:
- `ContradictionType.EXFIL_CORRELATION` added to `sift_find_evil/self_correction/contradiction_detector.py`.
- `ContradictionDetector.detect_save_then_exfil(mft_entries, emails, content_reader, window_seconds=300)` returns a list of `Contradiction` objects, one per matched (file, email) pair.
- Matching is hash-based: for each email attachment, find MFT entries whose content-hash equals the attachment hash AND whose `$STANDARD_INFORMATION.created` is within `window_seconds` before the email's `submit_time`. Fall back to `(filename, size)` match only when no content reader is supplied, and mark the confidence lower in that fallback path.
- `ConfidenceScorer` scores the new type starting at 0.95 for hash match, 0.65 for size+name fallback, with standard deductions for missing context (no recipient in headers, etc.).
- Findings emitted by this detector are tagged `FindingCategory.DATA_EXFILTRATION` (see SFE-7).
- Unit tests: hash match inside window, hash match outside window (no finding), size+name fallback, and header analysis flag for the external-recipient case.

title: Tune exfiltration confidence scoring by time delta
description:
Current implementation: Any file-to-email correlation <300s = 0.95 confidence (flat scoring). Consider graduated confidence based on time delta to better reflect certainty of intentional exfiltration vs automated processes:

**Proposed thresholds:**
- 0-60s: 0.95 (Very High) - Immediate exfiltration
- 60-180s: 0.90 (High) - Deliberate but not immediate
- 180-300s: 0.85 (Medium-High) - Could be manual or automated

**Rationale:**
Shorter time deltas indicate more deliberate action. A 10-second delta is stronger evidence than a 280-second delta. Automated backup/sync processes typically have longer, more consistent delays.

**Testing requirements:**
- Test against multiple M57 characters (Pat, Terry, Charlie, Jo)
- Validate thresholds don't create false negatives
- Compare against known-good exfiltration timings
- Adjust thresholds based on empirical data

**Current behavior:** Jean case (43.9s) would remain 0.95 under proposed scoring.
close_reason: Implemented graduated confidence scoring (0-60s=0.95, 60-180s=0.90, 180-300s=0.85). Updated validator to check threshold alignment. All tests passing.

description:
Current file carving searches for 8 signatures (JPEG, PDF, ZIP, PNG, GIF, EXE/DLL, LUKS, ELF). Expand signature library to improve recovery on wiped disk scenarios:

**Document formats**: DOCX (PK\x03\x04 + word/), XLSX (PK\x03\x04 + xl/), PPTX, RTF ({\rtf1), ODT
**Archives**: RAR (Rar!), 7Z (7z\xBC\xAF\x27\x1C), TAR, GZ (\x1F\x8B)
**Windows artifacts**: Registry hives (regf), Event logs (ElfFile), Prefetch (SCCA), MFT records
**Email**: PST (\x21\x42\x44\x4E), OST, EML (From:), MSG
**Databases**: SQLite (SQLite format 3), Access (.mdb header)
**Browser**: Chrome/Firefox SQLite DBs, cache files

Reference implementation in analysis/real_examples/wiped_disk/ uses Python + pytsk3 for signature scanning. Extend signatures dict in carving script.

value: Agent delegation patterns from deep audit: Use specialized agents for systematic quality work. doc-updater agent: Excellent for comprehensive docstring coverage - processes entire package methodically, follows Google-style conventions, fixes formatting issues (D212), generates 100+ docstrings in one session. tdd-guide agent: Strong for test coverage improvement - writes edge case tests, follows AAA pattern, creates fixtures, achieves 40%→100% coverage jumps on critical modules. When to delegate: (1) systematic work across many files (docstrings, tests), (2) specialized domain expertise needed (security, performance), (3) time-consuming but well-defined tasks. Provide clear success criteria, example formats, and target metrics in agent prompts. Agents work autonomously but verify results after completion (run pydocstyle, pytest --cov).

Thorough architecture documentation structure: Layer 1 (Evidence) - read-only handlers with integrity verification, explain tool choices (pytsk3 for NTFS, pypff for PST, tshark subprocess for PCAP). Layer 2 (Parsers) - frozen dataclasses, document data models with code, explain field choices (why SI and FN timestamps? why streaming SHA-256?). Layer 3 (Detectors) - describe algorithm steps with numbers (M57 Jean: 91,459 MFT entries filtered to 234 candidates via timeframe, hashed 228, found 2 matches), explain why it works (cryptographic proof + temporal signal). Layer 4 (Validators) - contradiction types with confidence impacts (-0.50 causality, -0.30 timestomping, -0.20 temporal mismatch, -0.15 missing artifact), resolution strategies (Event Log tiebreaker recovers +0.30). Layer 5 (Self-Correction Engine) - 6-step workflow (detect→contradict→resolve→score→reason→output), confidence levels with ranges (0.95-0.99 very high down to 0.10-0.29 low). Include data flow scenarios with timing and trade-offs.

Test coverage improvement strategy from deep audit: Prioritize modules with largest coverage gaps and highest criticality first. Target: 80%+ coverage overall. Focus on: (1) untested code paths (lines shown in coverage reports), (2) edge cases (null inputs, empty lists, boundary values), (3) error handling paths (exceptions, invalid data, corrupted files). Use AAA pattern (Arrange, Act, Assert) with descriptive test names. Mock external dependencies (disk images, PST files). Keep tests fast (<1s total) and isolated. Tools: pytest with pytest-cov, tdd-guide agent for systematic test writing. Example progression: exfil_detector 40%→100% by testing _filter_mft_by_email_timeframe (edge cases), _correlate_hashes (temporal proximity), hash computation (read errors), and full detect_exfiltration workflow. Result: 61%→69% overall, 3 critical modules at 100%, 203 tests passing in <1s.

Documentation best practices from deep audit: Use Google-style docstrings with one-line summary on first line (no D212 errors). Include Args/Returns/Raises sections for all public functions. For Protocol classes (duck typing), document each abstract method even if just a stub. Focus docstrings on WHY and WHAT, not HOW (code explains how). Add examples for non-obvious usage. For user-facing docs, provide complete workflows with commands, expected output (JSON samples), and troubleshooting. Use real datasets (M57 Jean, CIRCL) for examples. Include performance benchmarks. Structure: installation → quick start → concepts → workflows → case studies → troubleshooting → advanced usage. Tools used: pydocstyle for validation, doc-updater agent for systematic coverage.

Specific wins: M57 Jean + CIRCL real examples demonstrate capabilities better than synthetic demos, streaming SHA-256 pattern (64KB chunks) shows memory-conscious design, artifact-centric detection (no case-specific strings) shows forensic domain expertise. File carving on wiped disks: When filesystem metadata is destroyed, signature-based carving recovers files but loses critical context (filenames, timestamps, directory paths, permissions). For effective triage: 1) Hash all carved files immediately, 2) Compare against NSRL database to filter known-good system files (reduces 90%+ noise), 3) Submit unknowns to VirusTotal for malware identification, 4) Deep strings analysis on suspicious files for IOCs, credentials, attacker artifacts. Without NSRL database, manual triage becomes major bottleneck. CIRCL case carved 403 executables - likely mostly system DLLs but verification required 60-90 minutes due to VirusTotal rate limits and lack of NSRL filtering.
